blocks.text: ¹H NMR mein jis sample ko check karna ho use zyada solvent mein ghol kar solution banaya jata hai. Aam solvents mein hydrogen atoms hote hain jo tez signals dete hain aur sample ke spectrum mein rukawat (interference) dalte hain. Is masle se bachne ke liye deuterated solvents use kiye jate hain, jaise CDCl₃ (deuterated chloroform) ya CD₃OD (deuterated methanol). Agar aam CHCl₃ solvent ho to us ke akele proton (¹H) ka signal itna tez hoga ke sample ke protons ke kamzor signals bilkul chhup jayenge. CDCl₃ mein hydrogen (H) ki jagah us ka isotope deuterium (D) hai. Deuterium ko palatne ke liye radio waves ki mukhtalif frequency chahiye, is liye yeh sample ko di gayi radio frequency jazb nahi karta aur ¹H NMR spectrum mein is ki peak nahi aati. Is tarah solvent "khamosh" (silent) rehta hai aur spectrum mein sirf sample ke signals nazar aate hain.

blocks.prompt: ¹H NMR mein CHCl₃ ki jagah CDCl₃ kyun use hota hai?
blocks.explanation: CHCl₃ ke proton ka tez signal sample ke kamzor signals ko chhupa deta. CDCl₃ mein H ki jagah D hai, jo ¹H wali frequency jazb nahi karta, is liye solvent ki koi peak nahi aati.

items: Aam solvents ke hydrogen tez signals de kar sample ke signals chhupa dete hain.
Deuterated solvents (CDCl₃, CD₃OD) ¹H spectrum mein khamosh rehte hain.
